html:
In March and April 2017 French Guiana was shut down by a general strike and road blockades, the largest social movement in its history. Protesters demanded action on crime, health, schools and the cost of living.

The movement began with strikes in the electricity company and among transport workers, and grew when a collective of masked men, the 500 Brothers, called for action against crime in Cayenne. Roadblocks closed the main roads, schools and the port, and a rocket launch at the Guiana Space Centre in Kourou was delayed. Tens of thousands marched, in a territory of under 300,000 people.

It ended on 21 April with an agreement in which the French state pledged about one billion euros of emergency spending and promised more. The strike showed the gap between French Guiana and mainland France, despite its status as a French department.
sum: In March and April 2017 French Guiana was shut down by a general strike and road blockades, the largest social movement in its history. Protesters demanded action on crime, health, schools and the cost of living.
